_readme: WHAT THIS FILE IS: the list of AWS managed policies that mapping.json is allowed to attach to a permission set.

WHY IT EXISTS: without it, anyone who can edit mapping.json could give a group a powerful policy. A policy that is not listed here makes the checks fail in two places: in CI (the pull request cannot pass) and inside the Lambda (the run stops before it touches AWS).

HOW TO READ AN ENTRY: the key is the policy ARN. 'tier' is 'standard' (normal) or 'privileged' (powerful). A mapping rule that uses a privileged policy must include a written 'justification'. 'max_session_duration' is the longest sign-in session a rule using this policy may ask for (ISO 8601: PT4H means 4 hours). A privileged policy can never allow more than PT4H. 'reason' is why the policy is allowed, for the people reading this file.

NEVER ALLOWED: policies that control IAM, Organizations or Identity Center themselves (for example IAMFullAccess) are blocked in the code and cannot be allowed here. Listing one makes this whole file invalid.

HOW TO CHANGE IT: edit on a branch and open a pull request. Treat every new line as a decision to give people more power, and explain it in 'reason'. Adding a policy and using it in mapping.json should be separate, reviewable changes.
This file is plain JSON, which does not allow comments, so these notes live in the _readme key. The program ignores it.

arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess.reason: View-only access to AWS resources. Cannot change anything.

arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecurityAudit.reason: Read-only access to security configuration, for the security team.

arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/PowerUserAccess.reason: Lets engineers build and run workloads. Full access except managing IAM users and roles, so sessions are short and each rule must be justified.

arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAcc.reason: Full administrative access for the IT admin group, for break-glass and platform work. Shortest session of any policy, and each rule must be justified.
